tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List the Dactic agents you (the signed-in user) have deployed, newest first. Returns each agent's id, name, platform and status. Use load_agent to run one or get_agent for its details. Returns not_found when you have none.

tools.name: get_agent
tools.description: Get one of your Dactic agents by id: its name, platform, status, complete instructions and every skill (name, description, full procedure). Never returns another user's agent.

tools.name: load_agent
tools.description: Load one of your Dactic agents (by agent_id or exact agent_name) so you can run it in this chat: returns its complete instructions and skills. Follow them exactly. Returns not_ready when the agent has no approved instructions, and not_found when no agent matches; it never returns a partial agent.

tools.name: invoke_agent
tools.description: Run one of your deployed Dactic agents. Claude agents start a Managed Agent session; Monday agents are run by Monday's own board automation. The response always includes the agent's complete instructions and skills. Retrying the same request returns the same run instead of starting another.

tools.name: resolve_terms
tools.description: Look up what company-specific terms mean, from your organization's confirmed Dactic terminology only. Terms that aren't confirmed come back in gaps; never guess their meaning.

tools.name: check_freshness
tools.description: Is my Dactic knowledge up to date? Reports each surface (app sync, confirmed knowledge, terminology, approved playbook, department policies, skills, and optionally one agent) as fresh, stale, empty or unknown, with a recommendation for anything not fresh. tools.name: get_policy
tools.description: Get your department's current policies with their source document. With query: the policies that apply to it (all of them when your department has few, else the closest matches; coverage says which). Returns not_found when none are published.

tools.name: list_skills
tools.description: List your active Dactic skills (procedures derived from your interviews). disclosure_tier L1 returns a catalog; L2/L3 add the procedure. Use get_skill for one skill. Returns not_found when you have none.

tools.name: get_skill
tools.description: Get one of your Dactic skills by id, with its full procedure at disclosure_tier L3.

tools.name: ask_knowledge
tools.description: Answer a question from your own Dactic context: matches holds evidence from your synced work data and current department policies related to the question; your_profile holds your work context, skills, agents and connected apps. tools.name: search
tools.description: Search your Dactic knowledge (your skills, agents and approved playbooks, and your organization's confirmed terminology, plus current department policies). Returns results with an id, title and link; call fetch with an id for the full text.

tools.description: Fetch the full text of one Dactic item by the id search returned, with a link to it.

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description: Your Dactic AI usage (tokens by operation) over the last N days; scope=org is for org admins.

tools.name: get_sync_status
tools.description: Report recorded sync progress, last successful sync, approved source coverage and safe recovery guidance. Credential linkage is not proof of current access.

tools.name: get_feedback_status
tools.description: Follow the recorded processing/application state of your submitted agent feedback. No immediate agent change is implied.

tools.name: recommend_agent

tools.name: compare_agent_versions
tools.description: Compare two stored artifact versions of the same accessible agent/platform, with instruction diffs and skill additions/removals. Missing guardrails/parameters remain unknown. Never rolls back or deploys.

tools.name: find_context_gaps
tools.description: Assess task preparation using available knowledge, skills, policies, terminology and sync readiness. Returns blocking/nonblocking gaps; unknown requirements or execution permissions remain unknown.

tools.name: get_entity_context

tools.name: get_context_delta

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: load_agent, get_skill_usage · Private data: get_policy, get_user_context, get_knowledge_provenance, submit_agent_feedback, get_usage, get_sync_status · Public sink: submit_agent_feedback · Destructive: list_agents, load_agent, invoke_agent, check_against_policy, create_agent_from_process.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: load_agent, get_skill_usage · Private data: get_policy, get_user_context, get_knowledge_provenance, submit_agent_feedback, get_usage, get_sync_status · Public sink: submit_agent_feedback · Destructive: list_agents, load_agent, invoke_agent, check_against_policy, create_agent_from_process

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
